vidiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form of vidita with -iya ending, used in the Apadāna verse; probably 'found' or 'known'. Meaning uncertain.
vidiya.example_1: Hitvā papañce jitaphanditāni [vidiya phanditāni (sī.) jitabandhitāni (ka.)], tatheva bodhiṃ anupāpuṇiṃsu.
vidiya.translation_1: Abandoning obstacles, throbbing conquered, thereby indeed they achieved Awakening.

suññatappaṇīhitañcānimittaṃ.meaning_2: void, aspiration, and the signless; emptiness, wish, and nothingness
suññatappaṇīhitañcānimittaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of suññata, paṇīhita (with extra ppa, variant of paṇidhi? or paṇīhita) and animitta. The cī variant suññappaṇidhiñca tathānimittaṃ suggests reading suñña + paṇidhi + ca + animitta, i.e. 'void, aspiration, and signless'. Alternate analyses exist.
suññatappaṇīhitañcānimittaṃ.translation_1: 133. “In a Victor’s dispensation practicing merit, aspiration and thus gaining signs,

vijjalantā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it modifies dīpā, nominative plural masculine. It can be analysed as a compound (vi + jala + anta) or as a present participle of a hypothetical vijjalati. The related entry suggests the split vi+jala+a+anta.
vijjalantā.example_2: Dīpā parattha idha vijjalantā, paccekabuddhā satataṃ hitāme.
vijjalantā.translation_2: Lamps shining the light of ultimate truth here, these Lonely Buddhas are constantly honored.

lokasudakkhiṇeyyā.meaning_2: worthy of the world's good gift; worthy of the best offerings of the world; supremely worthy of the world's homage
lokasudakkhiṇeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of lokadakkhiṇeyya with the prefix su- (well; good). It is a bahubbīhi compound meaning 'one to whom the world's best gifts are due'. In the verse it is nominative plural in -ā, agreeing with paccekabuddhā. The PEU treats it as a ti (adjective) with the split loka + sudakkhiṇeyya.
lokasudakkhiṇeyyā.translation_2: Free of Doubt and Good for the World to Look At, these Lonely Buddhas are constantly honored.

vajalā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. syā.) for balajā (pī. jalajā) in a list of fish. Treated here as a feminine name of a fish; the form is nominative singular.
vajalā.example_1: 145. ‘‘ Pāṭhīnā pāvusā macchā, balajā [vajalā (sī. syā.) jalajā (pī.)] muñjarohitā;
vajalā.translation_1: Sheatfish, pāvusa, valaja, reed-fish, red-fish and maggura

vaggulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Spelling variant of vaggulī; nominative singular in the text. Some editions read vagguḷā.
vaggulā.example_1: Vaggaḷā [vaggulā (sī.) vagguḷā (syā.) maggurā (theragāthā)] papatāyantā, sobhayanti [papatāyanti, sobhayantā (ka.)] mamassamaṃ.
vaggulā.translation_1: are flowing with the current there, making my ashram beautiful.

aṅkolā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of aṅkola used for the flower; nominative singular in the text, listed among flowering trees in the assama.

uddhālakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Tree name in a list of flowering trees. Nominative plural in the text. Sometimes written uddālakā.
uddhālakā.example_2: 153. ‘‘ Uddhālakā ca kuṭajā, kadambā vakulā bahū;
uddhālakā.translation_2: Golden shower, winter cherry, kadam and Spanish cherry trees

kadalimātuluṅgiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in -iyo (or possibly plural). A compound of kadali (banana) and mātuluṅgī (citron).
kadalimātuluṅgiyo.translation_2: Ālaka and isimugga, banana, also citron trees

mulāḷiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form is nominative plural. √mul 1 (root, support) is a guess; the formation is uncertain, possibly a non-verbal loanword or from mūla (root).
mulāḷiyo.translation_2: Pink lotuses germinate there; the lotus roots are being cleansed.

siṃghāṭipattamākiṇṇā.meaning_2: strewn with siṃghāṭi leaves; covered with siṃghāṭi-palm leaves
siṃghāṭipattamākiṇṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of siṃghāṭi (a kind of palm/its leaf), patta (leaf) and ākiṇṇā (strewn, covered; fem nominative plural, agreeing with the subject). In the text it describes the tank (taḷāka).
siṃghāṭipattamākiṇṇā.translation_1: Singhāṭi leaves are strewn about, making that tank so beautiful.

uttalī.meaning_2: name of a plant (perhaps a river-branch flower); name of a flowering shrub
uttalī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in a list of plants; exact identification uncertain. Appears as uttalī in the text, but the English translation suggests uttuli. Probably a feminine ī-stem noun; nominative singular may be uttalī.

saṃgulā.meaning_2: fork-tailed catfish; a kind of fish
saṃgulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed in PEU as saṃgula (masc), a kind of fish, possibly a wrong sandhi for sakula; here nominative plural in -ā, listed beside maggurā. Doubtful reading, variant maṅgurā.
saṃgulā.example_1: Saṃgulā maggurā [maṅgurā (sī. ka.)] ceva, vasanti taḷāke tadā.
saṃgulā.translation_1: are living in that tank there then.

poṭṭhasīsā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a bird with a tufted or crested head, perhaps an owl or a peacock. Plural in the text (kosikā poṭṭhasīsā ca). Literally 'tuft-head'.
poṭṭhasīsā.example_2: 163. ‘‘ Kosikā poṭṭhasīsā ca, kurarā senakā bahū;
poṭṭhasīsā.translation_2: Owls and poṭṭhasīsas too, numerous hawks, also osprey,

rohiccā.meaning_2: rohicca deer; a kind of red deer; antelope
rohiccā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the text as rohiccā, which is nominative plural (the deer are said to live on the lake). Could also be taken as an abbreviation or scribal variant, but the PEU lists rohicca as a type of deer. If the reading is Rohiccā, it may be a proper name.
rohiccā.example_2: Rohiccā sukapotā [suttapotā (syā.)] ca, upajīvanti taṃ saraṃ.
rohiccā.translation_2: rohicca-deer, suggapotas are living on that lake there then.

āluvā.meaning_2: bindweed; potato plant; name of a plant
āluvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Part of a list of plants in the Apadāna verses. Also appears as āluva in other sources. Could be a feminine form of āluva.
āluvā.example_2: 170. ‘‘ Āluvā ca kaḷambā ca, biḷālītakkaḷāni ca;
āluvā.translation_2: Bindweed, also titan arum, bilāni, takkaḷāni bulbs jīvaka and sahaka plants

kaḷambā.meaning_2: titan arum (Amorphophallus campanulatus); a kind of plant
kaḷambā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of a list of plants and appears in compound with ca; possibly a variant of kaḍamba.
kaḷambā.example_2: 170. ‘‘ Āluvā ca kaḷambā ca, biḷālītakkaḷāni ca;
kaḷambā.translation_2: Bindweed, also titan arum, bilāni, takkaḷāni bulbs jīvaka and sahaka plants

ajjhogahiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular aorist, differing from the common ajjhogāhiṃ; sandhi of adhi + ava gives ajjho-. In the text vanaṃ is its object: 'I entered the forest'.
ajjhogahiṃ.translation_2: Taking ascetics’ requisites I proceeded into the woods.

maddasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular present of maddati; in the verse, addresses the Buddha and describes crushing heretics. The form maddasī has a long ī due to sandhi.
maddasī.translation_2: with that knowledge, Omniscient One, you crush rivals and heretics.”

accugato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ati + gata (ati > accu before g). Nominative singular masculine in the verse, describing the sea or a mountain. Sometimes analysed as accuggata.
accugato.translation_1: in the great ocean for as long as eighty-four thousand aeons.

olokayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist form olokayī (3rd singular) in the text. The present stem is olokayati; causative of √lok with prefix ava.
olokayī.translation_2: arising from his meditation, surveyed the whole world, that Victor.

nisiditvā.meaning_2: having sat down; having seated oneself
nisiditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā of nisīdati (ni + √sad). Sandhi -i- before -tvā. Used in the text of the Buddha sitting down in the monks' assembly.
nisiditvā.translation_1: sitting in the monks’ Assembly right then made manifest a smile.

aḷārapamhā.meaning_2: with dense eyelashes; having thick eyelashes; with long eyelashes
aḷārapamhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive bahubbīhi compound in a verse of the Apadāna describing women; nom. pl. fem. agreeing with the following adjectives (hasulā, susaññā, tanumajjhimā).
aḷārapamhā.translation_2: with long eyelashes, lovely smiles and slim waists, pleasant to look at,

phālaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the text ('should split'), not present indicative; translation treats it as optative after chetvāna. Causative of phalati (splits open).
phālaye.example_2: 272. ‘‘ Yathā sāratthiko poso, kadaliṃ chetvāna phālaye;
phālaye.translation_2: 272. Just as a man, wanting its pith, who chops and splits a banana tree,

paphussanti.meaning_2: come ashore; reach the shore; touch the shore
paphussanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular in a verse; some editions read phusanti instead. The prefix pa- is reduplicated in this reading; take the root as √phus 1 (touch).
paphussanti.example_1: Sabbā velaṃva phusanti [sabbāva velaṃ phusanti (sī.), sabbā velaṃ paphussanti (syā.)], sañcuṇṇā vikiranti tā.
paphussanti.translation_1: when they do come onto the shore, they are crushed to bits and scattered.

sañcuṇṇā.meaning_2: crushed to bits; ground to powder; pulverised; scattered
sañcuṇṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural in the text, agreeing with tā. Alternative form of sañcuṇṇita; sometimes analysed as saṃ + cuṇṇa + a.
sañcuṇṇā.example_2: Sabbā velaṃva phusanti [sabbāva velaṃ phusanti (sī.), sabbā velaṃ paphussanti (syā.)], sañcuṇṇā vikiranti tā.
sañcuṇṇā.translation_2: when they do come onto the shore, they are crushed to bits and scattered.

sañcuṇṇāva.meaning_2: as if crushed to powder; as though pulverised
sañcuṇṇāva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sañcuṇṇā (nominative plural of the past participle sañcuṇṇa, 'crushed to powder') with iva, 'like, as if'. In the text the phrase is sañcuṇṇāva bhavanti te, 'they become as if crushed to powder'.
sañcuṇṇāva.translation_2: having come into your presence, they get thoroughly crushed by you.

osadho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text. In the simile 'yathāpi selo himavā, osadho sabbapāṇinaṃ' the Buddha is likened to the Himalaya as a medicine for all beings; osadho may also be read as an adjective agreeing with selo.

nuloketvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading nuloketvā in the Ka. edition for anuloketvā (the first vowel elided after catuddisā). Absolutive in -tvā; the tense is past.
nuloketvā.translation_1: surveying the four directions then growls three times his mighty roar.

kittayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural aorist of the causative-denominative kittayati (from kitta, 'praise'), used with the accusative lokanāyakaṃ. PEU analyses it as kitta + ṇaya but the ending is aorist -uṃ.

sampamaddāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present tense, 3rd person singular. The form in the text sampamaddāmi is likely an irregular or metrical spelling; PEU gives it as caus. of sampamaddati.
sampamaddāmi.translation_2: 350. Today I’m the Dhamma’s general in the Buddha’s dispensation.

ussīsamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular ussīsamhi in the text. Possibly part of a compound meaning 'at the head' or 'on top'; cf. ussīsaka.
ussīsamhi.translation_2: Having called to mind my karma, Gotama, Bull of the Śākyas,

tūresu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the verse (vajjamānesu tūresu); the related tūriya is a metathesised form of the same word.
tūresu.example_2: 378. ‘‘ Vajjamānesu tūresu, devā tūrāni [turiyesu, devā turiyāni (sī. syā.)] vajjayuṃ;
tūresu.translation_2: 378. When the drums were being beaten, the devas then also beat on drums.

sampabujjhatha.meaning_2: wakes up; awakens; becomes fully awake
sampabujjhatha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the 3rd singular aorist(mid) form sampabujjhatha, an alternative ending to sampabujjhati; 'buddhopi sampabujjhatha' = 'the Buddha himself woke up'.
sampabujjhatha.translation_2: Upon hearing the sound of both, the Buddha himself then listened.

paghaṭṭenti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd person plural in the text; the causative stem paghaṭṭe- takes the ending -nti for the plural. Causative of pa + √ghaṭṭ (to strike, to hit).
paghaṭṭenti.example_2: Aññamaññaṃ paghaṭṭenti, ākiṇṇaṃ hoti laṅkataṃ [taṃ tadā (sī.), satatā (syā.), saṅkaraṃ (?)].
paghaṭṭenti.translation_2: where they gather, one another; the city was very crowded.

hatthissarathasaṃkulaṃ.meaning_2: crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots
hatthissarathasaṃkulaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a city (nagaraṃ). The compound ca is included in the Pāḷi as hatthī + assa. The form hatthis- stands in sandhi for hatthi-.
hatthissarathasaṃkulaṃ.translation_1: “Of such a sort was my city, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots.

brāhmaññakulasambhūto.meaning_2: born into a brahmin family; arisen in a brahmin clan
brāhmaññakulasambhūto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compounded form of brāhmaññakulasambhūto. A bahubbīhi describing a person; nominative singular masculine in the text.
brāhmaññakulasambhūto.translation_2: “Born into a brahmin family, I had a massive heap of gems.

pupphehacchādayī.meaning_2: covered with flowers; covered over with flowers
pupphehacchādayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pupphehi (instrumental plural of puppha) and acchādayī (aorist 3rd singular of acchādeti, 'covered'). The sandhi elides the initial a of acchādayī after the final i of pupphehi. Alternatively pupphehacchādayī could be pupphehi + chādayī, but the metre and the verb acchādeti favour the former.
pupphehacchādayī.translation_2: covered the entire Buddha-retinue with flowers at that time.

kittayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of kittayati (causative of √kitt). The final -ī is the aorist ending; the PEU split kittaṇaya is doubtful. Occurs only in verse, paired with sunandaṃ as the object.

kittayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative kitteti; the text has kittayi. Used with sambuddho and aggasāvakaṃ as the object.

kitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant kītvā, kitvā. Absolutive of kīṇāti/kiṇāti 'to buy'. In the text: 'having bought (the land) for a hundred thousand'.
kitvā.translation_1: I spent a hundred thousand coins and built that monastic ashram.

vikkhālayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist of vikkhāleti (causative of vi + √khal, 'wash, rinse'). The text has the -ayiṃ variant for -esiṃ. Object dose is accusative plural of dosa.
vikkhālayiṃ.translation_2: “Searching for the unconditioned, I washed away all of my stains.”

tāvadūraphale.meaning_2: whose fruit lasts that long; of such long-lasting fruit
tāvadūraphale.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative absolute in tāvadūraphale sati: 'while the fruit lasts so long; as long as the fruit endures'. Compound of tāva, dūra and phala; PEU glosses 'fruit lasting 1000 years'.
tāvadūraphale.translation_2: “The gods are looking after that as long as the fruit may last there.”

vijaṭayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text with the variant reading vijaṭayiṃ; the lemma is the aorist 3sg. The commentary relates it to balākānaṃ vijāyanūpamāya, so some take the reading vijanayiṃ (vijanati) instead. The PEU entry vijaṭaye suggests the same vi + jaṭa family.
vijaṭayiṃ.example_1: Caturo ca phale sabbe, dhammevaṃ vijanayiṃ [vijaṭayiṃ (ka.) balākānaṃ vijāyanūpamāya saṃsandetvā attho veditabbo] ahaṃ.
vijaṭayiṃ.translation_1: “emptiness, the absence of marks, suchness, intentionality.”

siṅghāṭaṃ.meaning_2: four-way junction; crossroads; (figuratively) court of law; bramble (Tribulus terrestris)
siṅghāṭaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears as siṅghāṭaṃ (accusative singular, and in the second verse nominative/accusative neuter); the PEU also gives neuter. The Apadāna uses it as a metaphor for the nine-fold teaching of the Buddha (dhammavīthi); 'court of law' is a contextual image.
siṅghāṭaṃ.translation_2: “Your court of law consists of the nine-fold teaching of the Buddha,”

vihārañcappaṇīhitaṃ.meaning_2: a dwelling place that is free from longing; a desireless abode
vihārañcappaṇīhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vihāraṃ (accusative of vihāra) and appaṇīhitaṃ (not directed towards anything, free from longing), the latter with elision of the initial a after the preceding -aṃ. Occurs in the stock list suññataṃ animittaṃ appaṇihitaṃ (emptiness, signlessness, desirelessness) in the Apadāna verse, where the edition reads vihārañca appaṇīhitaṃ. The sense 'desireless abode' depends on taking appaṇīhitaṃ as an adjective qualifying vihāraṃ.
vihārañcappaṇīhitaṃ.translation_2: “desirelessness and cessation: all of these form your Dhamma-hut.”

porohicco.meaning_2: royal advisor; domestic priest; the office of a royal priest
porohicco.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, describing Kolita (Moggallāna) as a royal priest by name.
porohicco.example_2: Kolito nāma nāmena, porohicco tavaṃ mune.
porohicco.translation_2: “Bearer of the ancient lineage, hard to approach, of mighty power,”

āsahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form in the text is āsahaṃ, 1st person singular present, 'I endeavoured; I was able', used in formulaic Apadāna verses. PEU's split ā+sahassa is unrelated.

sayambhumasādayiṃ.meaning_2: destroyed the Buddha existing by himself; crushed the independent Buddha
sayambhumasādayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st person singular of the causative sādayati (= sādheti, 'destroys'), with the object sayambhum 'the independently enlightened one' joined to the verb and assimilated before s-. The word is doubtful; some might read it differently.
sayambhumasādayiṃ.translation_2: ““We’ll bring our cities all to ruin; let’s seek the pardon of that sage.””

āsādito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used passively with mayā: 'the Buddha was attacked by me'. In the verse it describes the Buddha as provoked or assailed. Could also be read as aorist 1st singular āsādayiṃ, but the -a ending points to the participle.
āsādito.example_2: 561. ‘‘ Āsādito mayā buddho, ghoro uggatapo jino;
āsādito.translation_2: ““If we don’t make him understand, that Self-Tamed One, Self-Controlled One,””

sumekhalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of kings. Nominative singular in the text.
sumekhalo.example_2: 563. ‘‘ Sumekhalo kosiyo ca, siggavo cāpi sattako [sattuko (sī.)];
sumekhalo.translation_2: Sumekhala, Kosiya, Siggava, and also Sattaka;

āsādayitvā.meaning_2: having harassed; having insulted; having offended
āsādayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive; in the text used absolutely with isayo (seers), 'having harassed the seers'.
āsādayitvā.translation_2: having harassed the seers, they came to grief with their kingdoms.

sannipātayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative aorist, 1st person singular, from sannipātayati (saṃ + ni + pat, caus). The text has purise sannipātayiṃ, 'I assembled the people'.

mabraviṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular aorist, written with sandhi as mabraviṃ (= maṃ + abraviṃ) in the text; the variant idaṃ vacanamabravuṃ shows the 3rd plural abravuṃ in the same passage.
mabraviṃ.translation_1: falling down at the Buddha’s feet, they spoke these words:

abbhuggami.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of abbhuggacchati (abhi + ud + gam). In the text it takes nabhaṃ ('into the sky') as its object. The form abbhuggami is also found for the present stem in some analyses; here it is treated as aorist by context.

vācāsabhimudīrihaṃ.meaning_2: speech uttered by the bull among speakers (Sarabha); the noble speech uttered by him
vācāsabhimudīrihaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi or commentarial form, not resolved by rule. The sense of 'Sarabha' (sabha) and 'majestic speech' is uncertain; the sentence glosses it loosely.
vācāsabhimudīrihaṃ.translation_2: Having heard the words of the devas, that majestic speech they uttered,

upānayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of upānayati, used with bhikkhaṃ (alms), dhammasotaṃ (stream of Dhamma) and mahāmuniṃ (the great sage).

kappasagasse.meaning_2: cycle of aeons; series of aeons
kappasagasse.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text (kappasagasse). The related reading kappasahassa ('thousand aeons') also suits the context.
kappasagasse.translation_1: For thirty thousand aeons he will exercise divine rule.

ārūhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of ārūhati (ā + √ruh). In the verse ārūhi tañca nāvakaṃ it means 'climbed onto that boat'.
ārūhi.example_2: 631. ‘‘ Āgantvāna ca sambuddho, ārūhi tañca nāvakaṃ;
ārūhi.translation_2: When the Sambuddha had arrived, he climbed onto that boat.

nāvakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Diminutive of nāvā, the -ka suffix added to the feminine stem nāvā. Accusative singular in the text. The PEU entry treats it as feminine (thī) meaning 'noble boat'; the form here with -aṃ can be neuter nominative/accusative or feminine accusative.
nāvakaṃ.example_2: 631. ‘‘ Āgantvāna ca sambuddho, ārūhi tañca nāvakaṃ;
nāvakaṃ.translation_2: When the Sambuddha had arrived, he climbed onto that boat.

nāvasaṇṭhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a heavenly mansion (byamhaṃ). Accusative singular in the text; the compound is nāvāya saṇṭhitaṃ, 'standing like a boat'.
nāvasaṇṭhitaṃ.translation_2: A divine mansion will arise for you, well-made, boat-shaped;

parivimbhitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a corrupted or very rare reading; variant na honti parivimbhitā suggests parivimbhitā is an adjective agreeing with te, meaning 'equalled' or 'matched'. Not clearly from a listed root.
parivimbhitā.example_1: Sabbe te buddhanāgassa, na hontu paṇidhimhi te ’[na honti parivimbhitā (syā.), na honti paṇidhimhi te (ka.)].
parivimbhitā.translation_1: yet all of them are not equal to the might of the Buddha-elephant.

ekatthambhikattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Ekatthambhika; Ekatthambhika Thera's Apadāna
ekatthambhikattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ. Name of the elder Ekatthambhika from eka + thambha, 'one pillar'.

upacelā.meaning_2: Upacela; name of a universal monarch; name of four persons in a past aeon
upacelā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Irregular proper name (yādicchakanāma) used as a collective plural upacelā 'the four Upacelas' in the Apadāna verse; nominative plural in the text.
upacelā.translation_2: in the sixty-thousandth aeon, there were four named Upacela.

catusaṭṭhikkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of catusaṭṭhi and khattuṃ; the final -i becomes -i before kkhattuṃ. Adverb of number in the Apadāna verse.

kappeto.meaning_2: prepares; arranges; makes; forms; brings about
kappeto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the printed form kappeto is a variant reading for kappeti (3rd singular present).
kappeto.example_1: Gotamo nāma gottena, satthā loke bhavissati [yaṃ vadanti sumedhoti, bhūripaññaṃ sumedhasaṃ; kappeto satasahasse, esa buddho bhavissati;(ka.)].
kappeto.translation_1: called Gotama by clan, will be the Teacher in the world.

pasobhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Apadāna verse setacchatto pasobhito describes an elephant: 'with a white umbrella, adorned'. Alternative analysis: pp of pasobhati. Nominative singular; the related PEU entry gives pa + subha + ta.
pasobhito.translation_2: Adorned with a white umbrella, with trappings and a mahout,

sahatthipo.meaning_2: together with the elephant keeper; accompanied by a mahout
sahatthipo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes an elephant (hatthī) in a stock verse; nominative singular in the text. Sometimes written sahatthipo with sandhi -o.
sahatthipo.translation_2: Adorned with a white umbrella, with trappings and a mahout,

dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.meaning_2: ten and eight times; eighteen times
dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dasa + aṭṭha + khattuṃ. Alternative reading dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ. The commentary glosses dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ, i.e. eighteen times.
dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.example_1: 137. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ (sī.), dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, cakkavattī bhavissati;
dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.translation_1: Eighteen times he will be a Wheel-turning Monarch.

caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of aṭṭhakkhattuṃ; the c- belongs to the preceding dasa (dasa ca). Appears in verse as dasa aṭṭha caṭṭhakkhattuṃ, 'ten and eighteen times'.
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.example_1: 137. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ (sī.), dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, cakkavattī bhavissati;
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.translation_1: Eighteen times he will be a Wheel-turning Monarch.
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.example_2: 53. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (sī.), dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, devarajjaṃ karissati;
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.translation_2: “For ten and eight times he will exercise divine rule.

yārissati.meaning_2: whatever he will desire; whatever he will ask (for)
yārissati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of jhāyissati in the MIS cell; probably a faulty or unusual sandhi, perhaps yā + ārissati (√is 1) or ja + ārissati. Appears as a sandhi of a pronoun with a future verb, but the analysis is uncertain.
yārissati.example_1: Tathā sīlavihīno tvaṃ, na jhāyissasi [yārissati (syā.)] katthaci.
yārissati.translation_1: so you, without moral restraint, won’t be invited anywhere.

dammito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for dappita in the text; past participle used adjectivally.

abbhuggamī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of abbhuggacchati used with nabhaṃ ('rose up into the sky'). The PEU connects it with abhi + u + √gam; the ending -ī is the aorist 3rd singular. The related entry gives abbhuggami as the normalised aorist form.

ālagetvāna.meaning_2: having attached; having tied (to); having hung (on)
ālagetvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of a causative ālageti, used with a locative object (Veḷagge). The PEU split Ā+laga+tvāna suggests a simpler analysis, but the form points to a causative base.
ālagetvāna.translation_1: stuck it onto a bamboo pole, and raised a flag into the sky.

ussīsanti.meaning_2: are raised; are erected; are displayed
ussīsanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd person plural of a causative from √si with ud- and -sīsa-. Subject dhajā. Possible alternative analysis: passive of ussīsati. The PEU suggests a connection with ussīyanti.
ussīsanti.translation_2: flags were always seen by me for three leagues in all directions.

gopayiṃ.meaning_2: guards; protects; takes care of; preserves
gopayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular gopayiṃ in the text ('I guarded'). The PEU split 'gupa+ṇaya' is doubtful; the causative of √gup is more likely.

agopayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular in the text (agopayiṃ). From gopati; the initial a- is the aorist augment, not a negative prefix.
agopayiṃ.translation_2: For all that time, I guarded the refuge-going completely.

upasampādayi.meaning_2: ordained; conferred higher ordination (on); caused to attain
upasampādayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative upasampādayati (upa + saṃ + √pad, caus), used of the Buddha giving ordination; the PEU analysis upa+saṃ+pada+ṇaya+ī points to the same causative formation.
upasampādayi.translation_2: Knowing my virtue, the Eyeful One, the Buddha, ordained me.

suppaṇīhitaṃ.meaning_2: well directed; well disposed; well placed; well aspired
suppaṇīhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of su + paṇihita (pp of paṇidadhāti); the -ṇ- is doubled after the prefix su. Neuter nominative singular agreeing with mānasaṃ in the text.
suppaṇīhitaṃ.translation_2: 125. “Well-protected was my refuge, my mind well-placed.

parigopiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Gerund in -iya (see 130 in the text). Sometimes taken as an absolutive in -iya; the meaning is the same.
parigopiya.example_2: 130. ‘‘‘ Sammā dhammaṃ bhāvetvāna [mamopamaṃ karitvāna (sī. syā.)], sīlāni parigopiya;
parigopiya.translation_2: 130. “Rightly developing the Dhamma, guarding your virtues,

pañcasīlasamādāniyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the Elder Pañcasīlasamādāniya; title of a chapter; name of a sutta
pañcasīlasamādāniyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth chapter of the Thera-apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

saṃkittento.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of the causative saṃkitteti (√kitt + *e), used transitively. Masculine nominative singular in the text. Variant pakittento.
saṃkittento.example_1: 150. ‘‘ Saṃkittento ca [pakittentova (sī.), pakittente ca (syā.)] sabbesaṃ, abhimattañca porisaṃ;
saṃkittento.translation_1: Proclaiming this outstanding human action to everyone,

abhimattañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here in compound with porisaṃ (abhimattaṃ porisaṃ), probably 'overpowered human strength' or 'crushed manhood'. Form with -añca = abhimattaṃ + ca; the cpd. ending is separate, so this is a pp used adjectivally. Root √mad with ta-pp and assimilation d>t.
abhimattañca.example_1: 150. ‘‘ Saṃkittento ca [pakittentova (sī.), pakittente ca (syā.)] sabbesaṃ, abhimattañca porisaṃ;
abhimattañca.translation_1: Proclaiming this outstanding human action to everyone,

annasaṃsāvakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fifth chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

abhināmetvā.meaning_2: having bent towards; having inclined towards; having brought near; having invited
abhināmetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative abhināmeti (abhi + √nam). In the verse it describes respectfully directing or inviting the Buddha towards the meal; the PEU glosses 'bring (respectfully), to let droop/bend'.
abhināmetvā.translation_2: 157. Having invited the Sambuddha, I fed that great sage;

abhirūhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (abhirūhi, 'climbed aboard'), from abhirūhati; the sandhi before mahāmuni is not part of the word.
abhirūhi.translation_2: 173. Having heard my loud growling, the Great Sage climbed aboard.

ekañjalimakāsahaṃ.meaning_2: I made a single añjali (salutation with joined palms)
ekañjalimakāsahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of eka + añjaliṃ + akāsahaṃ (aorist 1st singular of karoti). The form is ekañjaliṃ akāsahaṃ with the final -ṃ of añjaliṃ assimilated to the following vowel; some editions read ekañjalimakāsiṃ. Compare the related ekañjalimakāsiṃ.
ekañjalimakāsahaṃ.translation_2: On seeing him, pleased and with happiness of mind, I pressed my hands together once.

pañcālīsītisataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Or pañcālīsītisata + aṃ; a numeral compound of 185, agreeing with gāthāyo in the verse.
pañcālīsītisataṃ.translation_1: One hundred and eighty-five verses have been spoken, all gathered together.

kadalīkaṇṇiṃ.meaning_2: banana bunch; sheaf of bananas; cluster of bananas
kadalīkaṇṇiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (kadalīkaṇṇiṃ). The stem is doubtful; probably shortened from kadalīkaṇṇikā for the verse, so the nominative may be kadalīkaṇṇī or kadalīkaṇṇikā. The PEU entry suggests kadalī + kaṇṇikā, a bunch of bananas.
kadalīkaṇṇiṃ.translation_2: I approached him, carrying a large sheaf of banana fruits.

ekādasañcakkhattuṃ.meaning_2: and eleven times; eleven times too
ekādasañcakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Word appears as ekādasañcakkhattuṃ in the text, sandhi of ekādasaṃ + cakkhattuṃ; some editions read ekādasakkhattuṃ without the sandhi.
ekādasañcakkhattuṃ.translation_2: He will be a king of gods for eleven times,

gāhayī.meaning_2: causes to take; makes take; hands out; distributes
gāhayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of gaṇhāti. In the text it is aorist 3rd singular with salākaṃ: 'made (them) take the ticket'. PEU also suggests gāheti (to look).
gāhayī.translation_2: the Victor sat in the Saṅgha of bhikkhus and had me take a ticket.

dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.meaning_2: ten and eight times; eighteen times
dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial phrase for the number of times, in the text dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ (dasa + aṭṭha + ca + kkhattuṃ) = 10 + 8 times = 18 times. The form dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ is a sandhi/contraction of dasa + aṭṭha + kkhattuṃ; the variant dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ gives the same sense with ca. Treated as an indeclinable numeral expression.
dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.example_1: 53. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (sī.), dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, devarajjaṃ karissati;
dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.translation_1: “For ten and eight times he will exercise divine rule.

cakkhūsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text cakkhūsi appears to be cakkhu + asi (2nd sg. of √as): 'you are the eye'. The form is glossed as 'eye' for all beings. Alternative analysis: sandhi of cakkhu + asi, but treated here as the noun cakkhu with enclitic verb.
cakkhūsi.translation_2: You are the eye for all, the dispeller of great darkness.

udakehaṃ.meaning_2: in water I; I in the water
udakehaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of udake (locative of udaka) and ahaṃ. The sandhi -e + a- > -e- may also be resolved as udake + ahaṃ with the a elided; the sense is 'I in water' (do not die). Appears in the Apadāna verse Udakehaṃ na miyyāmi.
udakehaṃ.example_2: Udakehaṃ na miyyāmi, āyāgassa idaṃ phalaṃ.
udakehaṃ.translation_2: I do not die in water; this is the fruit of an eating hall.

tisakkhattuṃ.meaning_2: thirty times; three times (in this context)
tisakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial numeral. In the verse it occurs with ahosi (aorist of hoti). Usually tisakkhattuṃ means 'three times' (ti + sakkhattuṃ), but here the context 'thirty times' may be intended (tiṃsa?).
tisakkhattuṃ.translation_1: I was a wheel-turning monarch, possessing the seven gems, thirty times;

dhammacakkikattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Dhammacakkika; title of a text in the Apadāna
dhammacakkikattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading, nominative singular in the text. The compound is built of dhamma, cakkika, thera and apadāna.

dhammacakkikattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Dhammacakkika; the ninth (chapter)
dhammacakkikattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth section of a chapter. Genitive therassa before apadānaṃ; therassa + apadānaṃ is a nasal sandhi. Stem of dhammacakkika is uncertain (kika suffix).

lasuṇado.meaning_2: garlic giver; donor of garlic; name of a previous Buddha
lasuṇado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a past Buddha in the Apadāna list. Nominative singular in the text; likely a bahubbīhi compound meaning "garlic-giver".

kapparukkhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of the tenth Thera in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.
kapparukkhī.example_2: Kapparukkhī ca dasamo, gāthā dvayadasasataṃ [gāthāyo dvādasasataṃ (sī.)].
kapparukkhī.translation_2: Kapparukkhī is the tenth; one hundred and twelve verses.

paṭisallituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of paṭisallīyati used after gacchate; written paṭisallituṃ with single l and t. The construction paṭi + saṃ + √lī is regularized to the common DPD form.
paṭisallituṃ.translation_2: being one bound to solitude, went off into seclusion.

anileritaaṅgaṇamhi.meaning_2: place not swept by the wind; unswept ground; dust-free place
anileritaaṅgaṇamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. The PEU analysis 'anilerita' as 'wind-blown' seems doubtful; better taken as na + īrita (not stirred/moved by the wind), agreeing with the English 'dust-free'. If analysed as anilerita + aṅgaṇa, the negative prefix belongs only to īrita.
anileritaaṅgaṇamhi.translation_2: “When the rain has fallen four inches, on grass in a dust-free place,

supaṇīhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is used in the singular with cittaṃ, meaning 'well-directed' in the sense of the mind being well-disposed or well-concentrated. The su+pa+ni prefixes stand for 'well-', 'forth-' and 'down-', i.e. 'placed/directed well'.
supaṇīhitaṃ.example_2: 51. ‘‘ Uttame damathe danto, cittaṃ me supaṇīhitaṃ;
supaṇīhitaṃ.translation_2: “Tamed in the ultimate taming, my mind is well-directed;

abhināmayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular with active ending -iṃ. Variant of abhināmesiṃ. In the text it takes the object saṅgharaṃ ('own house').
abhināmayiṃ.translation_2: with a pleased heart and happy mind, I led him into my house.

sannidhāpako.meaning_2: name of a thera; storer; keeper
sannidhāpako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a thera in the Apadāna; the text also has the variant sanniṭṭhāpako. Masculine nominative singular.
sannidhāpako.example_1: Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sanniṭṭhāpako [sannidhāpako (sī.)] thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.
sannidhāpako.translation_1: Thus indeed the venerable Sanniṭṭhāpaka Thera spoke these verses.

uggamī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of uggamati/uggacchati, here used of the Buddha rising into the air. Some texts read uggami; the ending -ī is the aorist 3rd singular.
uggamī.example_2: Uṭṭhāya sayanā [āsanā (sī.)] tamhā, vehāsaṃ uggamī jino.
uggamī.translation_2: Having risen from that seat, the Victor flew up into the air.

bodhayitvā.meaning_2: having awakened; having made known; having enlightened
bodhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative bodheti. In the text it stands at the head of a clause with bahū satte as object.
bodhayitvā.translation_2: the one with vision, having awakened many beings, will attain final nibbāna.

sopagato.meaning_2: gone to the bank (of a river); gone to the shore
sopagato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of so (bank; shore) and upagata (gone to). Nominative singular masculine in the text.
sopagato.translation_2: At that time, he, having approached, being incited by wholesome roots,

pupphagghiyamupānayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads pupphagghiyamupānayiṃ = pupphagghiyaṃ + upānayiṃ. The -ghiya is sometimes held to be a suffix form (puppha + ghiya); the compound analysis is given here.
pupphagghiyamupānayiṃ.translation_2: with a pleased mind and feeling happy, I offered that floral festoon work.

vivatthacchaddo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading vivatthacchaddo in the text; an epithet of the Buddha. Nominative singular.
vivatthacchaddo.translation_1: the Sambuddha with the covering removed, will arise at that time.

gandhodakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the Elder Gandhodakiya; Gandhodakiya Thera's Apadāna
gandhodakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The first element is the elder's name; its analysis is uncertain (possibly gandha + udaka + iya).

gandhodakiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the elder Gandhodakiya; Gandhodakithera's Apadāna
gandhodakiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth Apadāna in the Thera-apadāna. Nominative singular; a sandhi compound of three words, so stem and pattern are left empty.

asanabodhiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Asanabodhiya
asanabodhiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading; nominative singular neuter in -aṃ.
asanabodhiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Asanabodhiya Thera, the tenth.

ropayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of rohati. The form ropayiṃ is 1st person singular aorist, meaning 'I planted' or 'I established'. The sandhi form ropayiṃ is from ropayi + iṃ.

avopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Āvopupphiya Thera; Āvopupphiyatthera's legend
avopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a section of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

avopupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legends) of Elder Avopupphiya; Avopupphiyatthera's Apadāna (second)
avopupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the second Apadāna in a chapter, in the nominative singular. Sandhi of avopupphiyattherassa + apadānaṃ, with the following initial a elided after the preceding -a. avopupphiya itself is probably a proper name of an elder; the compound is a title, not a normal noun.

sindhuyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form is genitive singular of sindhu (the Indus River); the name of the river is sindhu, and the -yā ending is an alternative genitive singular. In these Apadāna verses sindhuyā nadiyā means 'of the Sindhu River'. The noun sindhu is masculine. The related entries sindhuja and sindhura are compounds with sindhu, not the same word.
sindhuyā.example_2: 13. ‘‘ Sindhuyā nadiyā tīre, cakkavāko ahaṃ tadā;
sindhuyā.translation_2: Back then, I was a ruddy goose on the bank of the Indus River;

susumpattiṃ.meaning_2: excellent attainment; great success; high prosperity
susumpattiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. syā.) for sukhasampattiṃ in the parallel line; probably a misreading or scribal variant of sukha + sampatti. Accusative singular in the text. Alternatively 3rd singular of no known verb.
susumpattiṃ.translation_1: I’ve come to know no bad rebirth (duggatiṃ): that is the fruit (phalaṃ) of praising him. I enjoyed no small quantity of happiness in good rebirths (sugatiṃ).

pupphacaṅkoṭiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya; Pupphacaṅkoṭiya Thera's Apadāna
pupphacaṅkoṭiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the tenth chapter of the Apadāna, nominative singular in the text. Thera's initial th is doubled after the preceding vowel. Contains the personal name Pupphacaṅkoṭiya.

pupphacaṅkoṭiyo.meaning_2: name of a monk; the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya ("flower-basket")
pupphacaṅkoṭiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a thera; nominative singular in the text. The name may mean "one who had a basket of flowers" (puppha + caṅkoṭi + ya).
pupphacaṅkoṭiyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā pupphacaṅkoṭiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

pupphacaṅkoṭiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya; Pupphacaṅkoṭiya's Apadāna
pupphacaṅkoṭiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna, nominative singular in the text ('dasamaṃ' = the tenth). The thera's name is pupphacaṅkoṭiya (with an 'ssa' genitive ending before āpadāna).

avopupphī.meaning_2: Avopupphī (name of a previous Buddha or distinguished person)
avopupphī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of names (Sakacintī, Avopupphī...). Doubtful form; possibly a corruption of a name such as Anomadassī. Treated as an irregular ī-stem; no reliable analysis.

parappasādī.meaning_2: who inspires confidence in others; whose faith others gain
parappasādī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A name (or epithet) in the list of previous Buddhas, given as 'Parappasādī' in the verse.

bhisado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a monk in a list of names in the Apadāna verses. Nominative singular in the text. Probably a compound (cf. bhisa, lotus root).

pupphacaṅkoṭakīpi.meaning_2: name of a deity (lit. flower basket)
pupphacaṅkoṭakīpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here the suffix -ī forms a name from the compound pupphacaṅkoṭaka (flower basket); the text has -pi ca joined to it. Nominative singular; the usual reading is Pupphacaṅkoṭakī.
pupphacaṅkoṭakīpi.translation_2: Ambadāyī and Sumano, and also Pupphacaṅkoṭakī,

bhisāluvañca.meaning_2: and the arum bulb; and the edible root
bhisāluvañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of bhisāluvaṃ (nt, probably bhisālukaṃ; edible root or bulb, likely of the arum or taro plant) + ca. Alternative split bhisālu + ca. PEU suggests bhisāluva = bhisa + āluva. Accusative singular in the text.
bhisāluvañca.translation_2: 14. I gave him edible roots and water to wash his hands.

pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Pāṭalipupphiya; Pāṭalipupphiya Thera's Apadāna
pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna. A sandhi of pāṭalipupphiyatthera and apadānaṃ; neuter nominative singular in the text.

ṭhitañjaliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Ṭhitañjali; the story of the Elder Standing with Folded Hands
ṭhitañjaliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text, as a heading.

tipadumiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Tipadumīya Thera; the story of the Elder Tipadumīya
tipadumiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the tenth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ; internal -iya- + thera- assimilate to -iyatthera-.

toṇi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a variant of toṇḍi (Damiḷa region name?) but here clearly a flower, perhaps a bud or blossom; sī. reading has uttamaṃ pupphaṃ, tīṇi pupphāni. Accusative singular in the text.
toṇi.example_1: Yaṃ tattha uttamaṃ toṇi, padmapupphāni [uttamaṃ pupphaṃ, tīṇi pupphāni (sī.)] aggahiṃ.
toṇi.translation_1: I picked up three flower-blossoms which were the foremost flowers there.

upanitehi.meaning_2: brought near; offered; presented; brought to
upanitehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural of upanīta, agreeing with me (by me). In the text rañño upanitehi me means 'offered by me to the king'.
upanitehi.example_2: 51. ‘‘ Kiṃ me imehi pupphehi, rañño upanitehi me;
upanitehi.translation_2: “What use are these flowers to me even if gifted to a king?

sampavattayuṃ.meaning_2: sets in motion; causes to arise; spreads; keeps going
sampavattayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist or plural form in the text (sampavattayuṃ) with ukkuṭṭhiṃ; taken here as the causative present stem. Could also be analysed as aorist of sampavattati. The PEU suggests a causative with vatu, but √vatt is more likely.
sampavattayuṃ.example_2: 55. ‘‘ Ye keci manujā disvā, ukkuṭṭhiṃ sampavattayuṃ;
sampavattayuṃ.translation_2: Whatever people saw them there then kept them thrown up in the air

tipadumānidaṃ.meaning_2: this is the fruit of the three lotuses; this fruit of three lotuses
tipadumānidaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ti + padumānaṃ (genitive plural of paduma) + idaṃ. The text's gloss 'three lotuses' fits tipaduma ('three lotuses') rather than ti + padumānaṃ; possibly tipadumānaṃ + idaṃ. Final member of the sentence.
tipadumānidaṃ.translation_2: I’ve come to know no bad rebirth: that’s the fruit of three lotuses.

tipadumiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Tipadumiya; Tipadumiya Elder's Apadāna
tipadumiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of Tipadumiya (the elder's name) + therassa (genitive singular of thera) + apadānaṃ (nominative singular). Title and colophon line, the tenth chapter or section of the Apadāna.

tipadumī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a Thera. The name means 'three lotuses'. Nominative singular in the text.
tipadumī.translation_2: Ṭhitañjalī, Tipadumī: five and seventy verses.

timirapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Timirapupphiya Thera; Timirapupphiya Thera's apadāna
timirapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the first chapter; nominative singular used as a heading.

adhopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Adhopupphiya; Adhopupphiyatthera-apadāna
adhopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading; nominative singular in -aṃ. The Elder's name is adhopupphiya ("one who offered flowers below").
adhopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Thera Adhopupphiya.

abhimatthayiṃ.meaning_2: moves towards; presses against; rubs; crushes
abhimatthayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the variant reading abhimatthayiṃ (1st singular aorist) is glossed as adhivattayiṃ, 'I moved towards'. The related entry abhimatthati and the gloss suggest √math with abhi.
abhimatthayiṃ.example_1: 24. ‘‘ Pakkhijāto viyākāse, pabbataṃ adhivattayiṃ [abhipatthayiṃ (syā.), abhimatthayiṃ (ka.), adhivatthayinti pabbatassa upari gacchintiattho];
abhimatthayiṃ.translation_1: Like a bird in the sky, I moved towards the mountain;

adhivatthayinti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text is adhivatthaṃ yiṃ, glossed by the edition as 'went over the mountain'. First person singular aorist.
adhivatthayinti.example_1: 24. ‘‘ Pakkhijāto viyākāse, pabbataṃ adhivattayiṃ [abhipatthayiṃ (syā.), abhimatthayiṃ (ka.), adhivatthayinti pabbatassa upari gacchintiattho];
adhivatthayinti.translation_1: Like a bird in the sky, I moved towards the mountain;

bodhimabhisiñcayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of bodhiṃ (accusative of bodhi) and abhisiñcayiṃ (1st person singular aorist of abhisiñcati). The contextual sense is sprinkling or honoring the Bodhi tree.
bodhimabhisiñcayiṃ.translation_2: In the ninety-one aeons since, when I watered that Bodhi Tree,

padumapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Padumapupphiya; Padumapupphiyatthera-apadāna
padumapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the start of the chapter. Nominative singular in -aṃ. The name Padumapupphiya means 'one who offered a lotus flower'.

aṭṭhatālīsamāsisuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural of aṭṭhatālīsamāsi; the text has aṭṭhatālīsamāsisuṃ, while the related entry has aṭṭhatālīsamāsi.
aṭṭhatālīsamāsisuṃ.translation_2: and in the eighteenth aeon there were forty-eight such monarchs.

timiranaṅgalīpuppha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of uncertain identification, apparently a flower name used as a personal name; the exact botanical referent of timira and naṅgalī is doubtful. Vocative in the text.

phalado.meaning_2: name of an ascetic; giver of fruit
phalado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a previous Buddha or ascetic in the Apadāna verses. The PEU analysis phala + dā + a is possible; the compound reading phala + da is preferred. Nominative singular in the text.

secako.meaning_2: name of a monk; sprinkler; one who sprinkles
secako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a monk in the Apadāna list of former lives; nominative singular in the text, possibly also an agent noun from secati (sprinkles).
secako.example_2: Dve raṃsisaññī phalado, saddasaññī ca secako;
secako.translation_2: two Raṃsisaññīs, Phalada, Saddasaññī, and Secaka,

sudhāpiṇḍiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Sudhāpiṇḍiya Thera; the life story of the elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya
sudhāpiṇḍiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna, not a word of the running text. The first element is probably sudhā + piṇḍi (sudhāpiṇḍi, 'ball of nectar'), with thera apadāna as a compound ending. Recorded as the nominative singular here, as in the heading; the text form lacks the final -ṃ.

idammattanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of idametamapi; idaṃ + mattaṃ (as far as this, only this much) + iti (marking the quoted limit). Appears in the phrase na sakkā puññaṃ saṅkhātuṃ.
idammattanti.example_1: Na sakkā puññaṃ saṅkhātuṃ, imettamapi [idammattanti (sī.), imetthamapi (ka.)] kenaci.
idammattanti.translation_1: no one can count the merit, saying 'it is this much'.

uparuci.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of kings. Nominative singular in the text.
uparuci.translation_2: Ruci and Uparuci, and Mahāruci was the third.

nibbūtikaṃ.meaning_2: with fires extinguished; with the fire (of defilements) quenched
nibbūtikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā.) for nibbutattaṃ/nibbutaggaṃ in this verse; accusative singular qualifying mahānāgaṃ. Probably a compound of nibbūta (pp of nir + √vā, 'blown out') + -ika, but the formation is uncertain.
nibbūtikaṃ.translation_1: the one whose fires are extinguished, the Great Elephant, like a thoroughbred bull,

tuvaṭṭāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular in the text: tuvaṭṭāmi = 'I lie down'. The root √tuvaṭṭ is rare; the PEU connects it with tuvaṭṭati / tuvaṭṭeti.
tuvaṭṭāmi.translation_2: 47. I lie down on my bed, on an ornamented mat of flowers;

veyyāvaccakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Veyyāvaccaka
veyyāvaccakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Muṭṭhipupphiya Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Muṭṭhipupphiya
muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ.

bījitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of vījitvā; bījati is a by-form of vījati. Absolutive in -itvā from bīja.
bījitvā.translation_1: Taking a garland of reeds, I bound it into a fan;

āsanupaṭṭhāhakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who attended to seats
āsanupaṭṭhāhakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

kalambāni.meaning_2: kalamba root; (according to commentary) a water creeper; a kind of amaranth eaten as a vegetable
kalambāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is accusative plural (kalambāni) as the object of khaṇantā, "digging up kalamba roots". The related entries kalambaka and kalambuka explain it as a water creeper (Ipomaea aquatica) or an edible amaranth.
kalambāni.translation_2: Digging up roots like kaḷamba, biḷāli, and takkaḷi too,

biḷālitakkalāni.meaning_2: biḷāli and takkala (roots); biḷāli and takkala bulbs
biḷālitakkalāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of biḷāli and takkala, names of edible roots or bulbs dug up as food. The text reads biḷālitakkalāni ca; the ending -āni is neuter plural. Uncertain identification of the plants.
biḷālitakkalāni.translation_2: Digging up roots like kaḷamba, biḷāli, and takkaḷi too,

udakado.meaning_2: name of a Paccekabuddha (or previous Buddha); (lit.) water-giver
udakado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Apadāna list of Paccekabuddhas; nominative singular in the text. Sometimes analysed as udaka + daha "pond, lake", but here it is a name.

ekāsaniyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Ekāsaniya; Ekāsaniya Thera's Apadāna
ekāsaniyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. The first member is the thera's name, Ekāsaniya.

upaṭṭhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of upaṭṭhāti (upa + √ṭhā), with ṭhā > ṭṭhā and the aorist ending -iṃ. The PEU analysis 'Upa+ṭhā+iṃ' agrees. In the text it takes the accusative objects bodhimuttamaṃ and saṅghamuttamaṃ.

suvaṇṇapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Suvaṇṇapupphiya Thera; life story of the venerable Suvaṇṇapupphiya
suvaṇṇapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fifth section of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

tetālīse.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ordinal number used in the stock aeon formula (ito kappe ...); locative singular in the text. The PEU entry suggests ti + catvāriṃsa with -ḍa, but the form is best treated as an indeclinable numeral.
tetālīse.translation_2: in the forty-third aeon before this, Wheel-turning Monarchs with great strength.

citapūjī.meaning_2: honouring the funeral pyre; worshipping the cremation mound
citapūjī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of cita (funeral pyre) and pūjī (honouring). Used adjectivally, likely describing a past life, but the exact sense is unclear. Commentators may explain cita as a heap or the sand pagoda.

sereyyavaggo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the thirteenth chapter (terasamo vaggo) of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

sereyyakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Sereyyaka Thera; Sereyyaka Thera's apadāna
sereyyakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Sereyyaka is the name of the thera.

sereyyakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. Probably a tree with fragrant flowers used in offering; the exact botanical identification is uncertain.
sereyyakaṃ.translation_2: Having taken up a Sereyyaka flower, I threw it up into the air.

vilāmālā.meaning_2: name of a female spirit; name of a goddess
vilāmālā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading vilāmālā (syā). The same sentence also has the variant cittamālā; the meaning is uncertain, but it looks like a proper name of a female being.
vilāmālā.example_1: Vītamalā [cittamālā (sī.), vilāmālā (syā.)] samānā ca, cakkavattī mahabbalā.
vilāmālā.translation_1: Vītamala by name, wheel-turning monarchs with great strength.

sereyyako.meaning_2: name of a monk; the elder Sereyyaka; Sereyyaka (maker of flower-stupas)
sereyyako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of an elder (thero) and the title of his verses in the Apadāna. It is also glossed 'pupphathūpī' (flower-stupa). Nominative singular in the text.
sereyyako.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sereyyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

sereyyakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of Elder Sereyyaka; Sereyyakatthera's Apadāna
sereyyakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter; nominative singular used as a heading (sereyyakattherassa + apadānaṃ, with -ssā- sandhi).

vāsayituṃ.meaning_2: to stay; to live; to dwell
vāsayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of vasati 1 (to live, stay). In the text with sālaṃ: 'to stay (beneath) the sal tree'. The PEU split vasa+ṇaya+tuṃ is doubtful; compare the causative vāsayati, but the meaning here is simply 'to stay'.
vāsayituṃ.example_2: Byādhinā pīḷito santo, sālaṃ vāsayituṃ gamiṃ.
vāsayituṃ.translation_2: Being afflicted by that illness, I went to stay beneath a sal tree.

saṃcari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (saṃcari = saṃcari); lemma given as present 3rd singular.
saṃcari.translation_1: 46. “And when that one was being born, the flocks of birds did not move;

vilokayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (vilokayi); the present is viloketi. The PEU entry analyzes it as vi + loka + ṇaya + ī, but this looks like an over-analysis.
vilokayi.example_2: 50. ‘‘‘ Jātamatto ca sambuddho, disā sabbā vilokayi;
vilokayi.translation_2: 50. “And when the Sambuddha was born, he looked in all directions;

saṃvejayitvā.meaning_2: having stirred; having moved emotionally; having inspired awe; having urged
saṃvejayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative saṃvejeti. Written saṃvejayitvā with the y glide. In the text it describes stirring up the crowd before praising the Buddha.
saṃvejayitvā.translation_2: 51. “Having moved the generations, and having praised the Leader of the World,

duddasi.meaning_2: name of a Buddha or aeon; (possibly) hard to see; having a bad view
duddasi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text (v.l. for pathavīdundubhi), probably a proper name. Could also be analysed as du + dasi or du + dassi, 'hard to see; having bad sight/views'. Locative/ablative singular in the phrase ekūnanavutimhito.
duddasi.translation_1: 54. “In the eighty-ninth aeon before this, Pathavīdundubhi by name,

agginibbāpano.meaning_2: name of a king of the universe; extinguisher of fire
agginibbāpano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a king of the universe in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.
agginibbāpano.translation_2: 57. “Agginibbāpana by name, in the eighty-sixth aeon,

vilokano.meaning_2: name of a king; (lit.) looking at; observing
vilokano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a former king in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.
vilokano.translation_2: 62. “The king Vilokana by name, in the eighty-first aeon,

gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Gaṇṭhipupphiya; Gaṇṭhipupphiya Thera's Apadāna
gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter of the Apadāna, occurring in the text as a heading. Nominative singular in -aṃ.

pupphathūpi.meaning_2: name of a monk; (lit. flower stupa)
pupphathūpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of an arahant monk in the Apadāna. The PEU glosses it as pupphathūpiya and connects the name to offering flowers (puppha) to a stupa (thūpī).

āsani.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of one of the paccekabuddhas in the Apadāna verse (āsani phalasaññī ca). Appears to be a feminine i-stem variant of āsana; feminine gender is uncertain.
āsani.translation_2: Āsani, Phala, and Saññī, Gaṇṭhi, and Padumapupphiya;

abhipūjemi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative form used with present meaning. First person singular abhipūjemi in the text, taking taṃ ñāṇaṃ as object.
abhipūjemi.translation_2: I revere that knowledge, O Best Buddha, O Great Sage.”

candanapūjanakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Candanapūjanaka Thera; the life story of the elder who honoured with sandalwood
candanapūjanakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading a chapter of the Apadāna. Candanapūjanaka is an epithet of the thera: 'one who honoured (the Buddha) with sandalwood'. Nominative singular in the text.

rohaṇī.meaning_2: name of a female deity; name of a goddess
rohaṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a deity (Rohaṇī) in the Apadāna verse; the name may also be a place or constellation name. Feminine ī-stem.
rohaṇī.example_2: Rohaṇī nāma [rohitā nāma (sī.), rohiṇī nāma (syā.)] nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalā.
rohaṇī.translation_2: all known by the name Rohiṇi, wheel-turning monarchs with great strength.

campakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of the Elder Campakapupphiya; Campakapupphiyatthera's legend
campakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the sixth section of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text; sometimes printed with a final -ṃ.

paricāriṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular aorist (paricāriṃ) of paricāreti, causative of paricarati. The form paricārayiṃ is also found; paricāriṃ could alternatively be analysed as an aorist of paricarati itself. Object vināyakaṃ is accusative singular.
paricāriṃ.translation_2: 69. Depending on that, I waited on the Guide;

atichattiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Atichattīya; Atichattīya Thera's Apadāna
atichattiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the Atichattīyattheraapadāna, nominative singular in -aṃ.

thūpasīkhasanāmakā.meaning_2: named Thūpasīkha; called Thūpasīkha; with the name Thūpasīkha
thūpasīkhasanāmakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a group of ninety-four aeons' worth of kings (or a Buddha-to-be) in the Apadāna. Nominative plural in the text. The PEU analysis (Thūpasīkha + samāna + nāma + ka, 'whose name is like the pinnacle of a pagoda') is doubtful; the simple split thūpasīkha + nāma + ka fits the verse better.
thūpasīkhasanāmakā.translation_2: In the ninety-four aeons since, known by the name Thūpasikha,

umāpupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna.

vaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the elder Vaṭaṃsakiya; Vaṭaṃsakiyatthera-apadāna (the ninth chapter)
vaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a chapter in the Apadāna; accusative singular as a heading.
vaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The ninth is the legend of Vaṭaṁsakiyatthera.

ajjhogahi.meaning_2: plunged into; entered; immersed oneself in
ajjhogahi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular aorist; ajjho- is the sandhi of adhi + ava. In the text it governs mahāvanaṃ (accusative).

parivārumapupphiyo.meaning_2: name of an arahant; one who offered a parivāruma flower
parivārumapupphiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet used of an arahant in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The first element parivāruma is doubtful, probably a flower name.

tambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The name Tambapupphiya is itself a compound (tamba + pupphiya, "copper-coloured flower"); thera means elder and apadāna means legend or biography.
tambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Elder Tambapupphiya

saṃthusito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for saṃthusito in the text; nominative singular agreeing with ahaṃ.

vīthisammajjakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Vīthisammajjaka; the Apadāna of the Elder Vīthisammajjaka
vīthisammajjakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title line of the third Apadāna in the text. Nominative singular in -aṃ.
vīthisammajjakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: 3. The Legend of the Elder Vīthisammajjaka

kadambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kadambapupphiya; Kadambapupphiya Thera's apadāna
kadambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text (subject of the chapter title). Kadambapupphiya is the name of the Elder; the final element is apadāna.
kadambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Kadambapupphiya Thera, the sixth (chaṭṭhaṃ).

tiṇasūlakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Tiṇasūlaka; title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna
tiṇasūlakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title, nominative singular in the text. Tiṇasūlaka is the elder's name; apadāna means legend or life story.
tiṇasūlakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Tiṇasūlaka Thera, the seventh (sattamaṃ).

nāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Nāgapupphiya; the Apadāna of Nāgapupphiya Thera
nāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Nāgapupphiya is the name of the Elder; apadāna means legend or life story.

punnāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Punnāgapupphiya Thera; the Apadāna story of the Elder Punnāgapupphiya
punnāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the ninth Apadāna chapter/sutta; nominative singular in -ṃ.

kadambī.meaning_2: name of a tree (Nauclea cadamba); kadamba tree
kadambī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of kadamba, used as a tree name in a list of flowering trees. Nominative singular in the text; could also be read as a proper name of a tree deity or nymph.

supāricariyo.meaning_2: Supāricariya; name of a monk; (lit.) one who is well served or easy to attend on
supāricariyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a thera (the author of these verses in the Apadāna). Nominative singular in the text. The PEU suggests the underlying compound su + pari + cara + ṇya; the form is more likely su + pāricariya, 'well served'.
supāricariyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā supāricariyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

kaṇaverapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kaṇaverapupphiya; Kaṇaverapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
kaṇaverapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the second chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

desapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Desapūjaka; title of a chapter
desapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the start of the chapter. Nominative singular in -ṃ. A compound of four members: desa (land), pūjaka (honouring), thera (elder), apadāna (legend).

kaṇikārachattiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kaṇikārachattiya; Kaṇikārachattiya Thera's Apadāna
kaṇikārachattiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Heading of chapter 5 of the Apadāna. A sandhi of kaṇikārachattiyatthera (name of an elder) and apadānaṃ (legend; title of a text). Could also be analysed as a compound kaṇikārachattiya + thera + apadāna.

yūthikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the Elder Yūthikapupphiya; the Apadāna portion on Thera Yūthikapupphiya
yūthikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A chapter heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.
yūthikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The seventh legend of Yūthikapupphiya Thera.

yūthikapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Yūthikapupphiya; Elder Yūthikapupphiya's Apadāna
yūthikapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of yūthikapupphiyattherassa + apadānaṃ. Title at the end of a chapter; nominative singular in the text. In the second sentence the text has dasamaṃ with sattamaṃ in the first.

pañcaṅguliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Pañcaṅguliya Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Pañcaṅguliya
pañcaṅguliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the tenth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Pañcaṅguliya is the name of the elder.

supāricari.meaning_2: name of a Pacceka Buddha; Supāricari
supāricari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Apadāna verse list of Pacceka Buddhas. The PEU suggests su + pari + cara + ṇya, an alternative nominal derivation, but here it functions as a name.
supāricari.translation_2: Supārī and Kaṇaverī, Khujjaka and Desapūjaka,

rattipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Rattipupphiya Thera; biography of the elder Rattipupphiya
rattipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

āsayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of āsu (aorist of √as) at Apadāna 24; here āsayuṃ is glossed as 'there were'. 3rd plural aorist.
āsayuṃ.example_1: 24. ‘‘ Pannarasasahassamhi, kappānaṃ aṭṭha āsu te [aṭṭha āsayuṃ (ka.)];
āsayuṃ.translation_1: In the fifteen-thousandth aeon, there were eight,

ekadīpiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Ekadīpiya Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Ekadīpiya
ekadīpiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

udapānado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name in the list of Paccekabuddhas; nominative singular in the text. Literally 'well-giver', from udapāna + √dā.

maṇippado.meaning_2: name of a Buddha; name of an ascetic
maṇippado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name occurring in a list of names in the Apadāna verses. Nominative singular in the text, in apposition to ekadīpī.

kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Kuṭajapupphiya Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Kuṭajapupphiya
kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the first chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

saṃvitthatasamotthataṃ.meaning_2: spread out and covered (with blossoms); well diffused and overspread
saṃvitthatasamotthataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound describing a flowering kuṭaja tree; accusative singular agreeing with kuṭajaṃ in the verse.
saṃvitthatasamotthataṃ.translation_2: On seeing a winter cherry tree, blossoming, well spread out and covered in flowers,

koṭumbariyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Koṭumbariya Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Koṭumbariya
koṭumbariyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading, nominative singular; the text abbreviates the name (perhaps Koṭumbariya or Koṭumbara).

koṭumbarasamākulaṃ.meaning_2: full of koṭumbara flowers; crowded with koṭumbara blossoms; thickly covered with koṭumbara
koṭumbarasamākulaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive to a flowering grove or tree in the Apadāna verse; accusative singular agreeing with the following noun. The PEU's 'cloth made in Koṭumbara country' is doubtful; the context is blossoms (pupphāni).
koṭumbarasamākulaṃ.translation_2: Lifting up seven flowers, filled with Koṭumbara blossoms,

koṭumbariyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Koṭumbariya; Koṭumbariya Thera's Apadāna
koṭumbariyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of the title koṭumbariyattherāpadānaṃ; the text has ttherassāpadānaṃ. Final word of the verse, nominative singular neuter.

buddharaṃsyābhiphuṭṭhomhi.meaning_2: touched by the Buddha's rays; illuminated by the Buddha's radiance
buddharaṃsyābhiphuṭṭhomhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of buddharaṃsīhi abhiphuṭṭha; the text has the alternative reading buddharaṃsīhi phuṭṭha. Used impersonally with amhi: 'I am touched by ...'.
buddharaṃsyābhiphuṭṭhomhi.translation_1: Touched by the Buddha’s rays, I offered them to the Best Biped.

isimuggadāyakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who gave a mugga-bean to the sage; title of the fifth Apadāna
isimuggadāyakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a text, nominative singular in the heading. Compound of isi, mugga, dāyaka, thera and apadāna.
isimuggadāyakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of Isimuggadāyaka Thera, the fifth.

tikaṇṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya; the story of the elder who offered three kaṇṇi flowers
tikaṇṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Compound of the elder's name Tikaṇṇipupphiya (tikaṇṇi + pupphiya, 'three kaṇṇi flowers') with thera and apadāna.

kiṃkaṇipupphaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of puppha with the flower name kiṃkaṇi; the spelling variant tikaṇṇipupphaṃ appears at verse 47. Accusative singular in the text.

tikaṇṇipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya; the eighth (chapter)
tikaṇṇipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A text title and heading: tikaṇṇipupphiyattherassa (genitive of the elder's name) + apadānaṃ. aṭṭhamaṃ in the sentence means 'the eighth (chapter)'.

tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Tivaṇṭipupphiya Thera; the Apadāna of Elder Tivaṇṭipupphiya
tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the tenth chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.
tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Tivaṇṭipupphiya Thera, the tenth.

teraseto.meaning_2: from the thirteenth; in the thirteenth (aeon)

tivaṇṭipupphiyo.meaning_2: named after offering three-stalked flowers; Tivaṇṭipupphiya (name of a monk)
tivaṇṭipupphiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a thera in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.
tivaṇṭipupphiyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā tivaṇṭipupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

tivaṇṭipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of therassa + apadānaṃ (the -a + a- elides to -ā-). Title at the end of a chapter; nominative/accusative singular neuter. tivaṇṭi + puppha + thera + apadāna.

koṭumbarikahatthiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a Paccekabuddha; a compound of two names. Nominative singular in the verse.

tivaṇṭi.meaning_2: having three sections; consisting of three parts (a chapter of verses)
tivaṇṭi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a chapter (vagga) of verses. In the text it is a nominative singular adjective, likely short for tivaṇṭivagga. The second element vaṇṭi is of uncertain form (possibly vaṭṭa or vaṇṭa); treated as an indeclinable compound.

tamālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Tamālapupphiya; Tamālapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
tamālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text, though it functions as a heading.

khaṇḍapulliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Khaṇḍapulliya Thera; the Apadāna of Khaṇḍapulliya Thera
khaṇḍapulliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Khaṇḍapulliya is the name of the thera.
khaṇḍapulliyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The third legend of Khaṇḍaphulliya Thera.

khaṇḍaphulliyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of an elder, nominative singular in the text. The related entry gives the base as khaṇḍaphulla + iya with the same meaning.

aṅkolakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Aṅkolaka Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Aṅkolaka
aṅkolakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading, nominative singular. The word is a compound of the monk's name Aṅkolaka, thera and apadāna.
aṅkolakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The fifth legend of Aṅkolaka Thera.

āseko.meaning_2: name of a king (Devagajjita); name of a former life of the Buddha
āseko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. The spelling may be a variant of āsaka or a name formed from √sic; uncertain.

virohano.meaning_2: growing tall; causing growth; making trees grow
virohano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a well or spring that makes the trees around it grow tall. Nominative singular in the text.
virohano.translation_2: There was a water well there, and trees growing tall.

kiṃkaṇikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya
kiṃkaṇikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter; nominative singular in the text.

yūthikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; often neuter in this compound with puppha, though the PEU guide lists it as masculine (yūthikā + a).

khaṇḍaphulli.meaning_2: name of a mountain (or dwelling place); Khaṇḍaphulli
khaṇḍaphulli.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed among the ascetic's dwelling places (asokiya, tamālatiṇasanthāra) in the Apadāna; perhaps a place name. Could also be a variant of the personal name Khaṇḍaphulliya.

sereyyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of Pacceka Buddhas. Nominative singular in the text.
