gāthāni.example_2: Chasatāni ca gāthāni, chasaṭṭhi ca tatuttari.
gāthāni.translation_2: There are six hundred verses and sixty-six more than that.

kaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kaṇikārapupphiya; Kaṇikārapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
kaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title used as a heading. Nominative singular in the text.

minelapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Minelapupphiya
minelapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ.

minelapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Minelapupphiya (the second)
minelapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title line of a sutta in the Apadāna. Sandhi of thetherassa + apadānaṃ with elision of the initial a. Could also be read as a compound of minela + pupphiya + thera + apadānaṃ in the commentary style.

kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kiṅkaṇipupphiya; Kiṅkaṇipupphiya's apadāna
kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text, used as a heading rather than as part of a sentence.

dahamoggayha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here in the compound dahaṃ + ogayha (“having plunged into a lake”); accusative singular daham. The text should probably be read as dahaṃ ogayha.

sināyi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text used with the sense 'bathed' (sināyi lokanāyako). The form is alternatively analysed as aorist of sināyati; the PEU treats it as an aorist with -ī.
sināyi.translation_2: plunging into a water-tank, the world's chief leader bathed.

taraṇiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Taraṇiya; the Apadāna story of the Elder Taraṇiya
taraṇiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the start of the Taraṇiyattheraapadāna section. Nominative singular; final -ṃ belongs to the case ending.

nigguṇḍipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of section 5 of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text (with niggahīta).

salalamāliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of the Elder Salalamāliya; the Apadāna of the Elder Salalamāliya
salalamāliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna. Salala is probably a variant spelling of salaḷa (the salaḷa tree), but the reading is uncertain; the PEU divides the compound slightly differently.

salalamāliyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the apadāna of the Elder Salalamālī; Salalamāliyatthere's apadāna
salalamāliyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna. The text form is nominative singular; sandhi of therassa + apadānaṃ. Sometimes written Salalamāliyatthere's.

koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya; Koraṇḍapupphiya Thera's apadāna
koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Koraṇḍapupphiya is the name of an Elder (thera), from koraṇḍa + puppha, 'koraṇḍa flower'.

koraṇḍapupphiyo.meaning_2: name of a Thera; the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya (who offered koraṇḍa flowers)
koraṇḍapupphiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of an arahant in the Apadāna, formed from the flower he offered (koraṇḍa). Nominative singular in the text.
koraṇḍapupphiyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā koraṇḍapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.
koraṇḍapupphiyo.example_2: Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā koraṇḍapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo
koraṇḍapupphiyo.translation_2: Thus indeed the venerable Koraṇḍapupphiya Thera

koraṇḍapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya
koraṇḍapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna, occurring with ordinal numbers (aṭṭhamaṃ, pañcamaṃ, tatiyaṃ). Nominative singular in -aṃ. The compound contains koraṇḍa + pupphiya (a flower-offering name), thera + ssāpadāna (with ssa as a sandhi form of the genitive therassa + apadāna).

dakado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of daka (water) + da (giving). Used as an epithet or name in the Apadāna verse; nominative singular in the text.

salalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in a list of tree names (also kuraṇḍaka). Nominative singular in the text; PEU also records a neuter sense "porcupine quill".

madadiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text has madadiṃ, probably mā adadiṃ ('I did not give') or a sandhi of maṃ adadiṃ. The commentary glosses dāna. Aorist 1st singular. The reading is uncertain.
madadiṃ.example_2: 3. ‘‘ Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ nāga [dāna (sī. ka.)] madadiṃ tadā;
madadiṃ.translation_2: In the ninety-four aeons since I gave that elephant at that time,

sitaraṃsiṃ.meaning_2: like the sun with cool rays; like the cold-rayed (sun)
sitaraṃsiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for sataraṃsiṃ; some editions read sītaraṃsiṃ (BSk). Accusative singular in the simile, after va. Analysis sita (cool, white) + raṃsiṃ (ray), or sandhi of sīta + raṃsiṃ.
sitaraṃsiṃ.example_1: 21. ‘‘ Udentaṃ sataraṃsiṃva, pītaraṃsiṃva [sitaraṃsiṃ va (sī. syā.)] bhāṇumaṃ;
sitaraṃsiṃ.translation_1: “Like the rising hundred-rayed sun, like the sun with cool rays,

anusaṃsāvayiṃ.meaning_2: causes to follow; escorts; sends after; accompanies
anusaṃsāvayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist first person singular anusaṃsāvayiṃ in the text, from the causative of anusaṃsavati; the PEU entry gives anusaṃsāvayati. Possibly 'I escorted / accompanied'.

tutideva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading; the parallel texts have jutideva or dutideva. The commentary (ka.) form has the same spelling; probably a corruption of a proper name (Jutideva / Dutideva). If taken as a name, the entry would be masc, comp.
tutideva.example_1: 49. ‘‘ Ito sattarase kappe, jutideva [dutideva (syā.), tutideva (ka.)] sanāmako;
tutideva.translation_1: “In the seventeenth aeon hence, there was one named Jutideva,

pāpanivārī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a thera in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.
pāpanivārī.translation_2: Sappi and Pāpanivārī, consist of fifty-four verses.

nipuṇavedanī.meaning_2: whose understanding is subtle; of keen perception; one who knows subtle things
nipuṇavedanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the predicate of paññā (nominative singular feminine agreeing with paññā). Sometimes analysed as nipuṇa + vida(√vid) + yu + ṇi, but here treated as a compound.
nipuṇavedanī.translation_2: My body is soft and my wisdom has a sharp intellect.

aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya
aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading, nominative singular in -aṃ. A three- or four-part compound: aṅkola (the aṅkola tree), pupphiya (relating to flowers), thera (elder), apadāna (legend).

aṅkolapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (story of attainment) of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya; Aṅkolapupphiya's Apadāna
aṅkolapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] It is a sandhi of aṅkolapupphiyassa, therassa and apadānaṃ. It is also the title of the Apadāna chapter. Nominative or accusative singular in the text.

sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya
sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

miñjavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya
miñjavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The personal name Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya is of uncertain analysis.

sukatāveḷiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Sukatāveḷiya; the life story of the Elder Sukatāveḷiya
sukatāveḷiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of two or more full words (sukatāveḷiyatthera + apadāna); title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text, written as one word.

bakuḷaṃ.meaning_2: Bakula tree (Mimusops elengi); fragrant flowering tree
bakuḷaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of bakula; accusative singular in the text as a list item. The tree is named among fragrant trees.
bakuḷaṃ.translation_1: Abyādhi, Aṅkola, Soṇṇa, Miñja, Āveḷa, and Vandana;

sālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Sālapupphiya; the biography of the elder named Sālapupphiya
sālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third chapter of the Sālapupphiyattheraapadāna in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. The compound name sālapupphiya means 'one who offered sāla flowers'.
sālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Elder Sālapupphiya, the third.

piyālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who offered piyāla flowers
piyālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh section of the Apadāna, a verse text. Nominative singular in the text.

tuvaradāyakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Tuvaradāyaka may be a proper name meaning 'giver of millet' (tuvarā).

tuvaranti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text's tuvaranti is read by the commentary as a form of tuvara (pigeon pea), i.e. 'they call it tuvara'; as a verb it would be 3rd plural of tuvarati. Doubtful.
tuvaranti.example_1: Bharitvā tuvaramādāya [bharitvā turavamādāya (ka.), bhajjitaṃ tuvaramādāya (?) ettha tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ tuvaraṭṭhinti tadaṭṭhakathā; tuvaro dhaññabhedeti sakkatābhidhāne], saṅghassa adadiṃ ahaṃ.
tuvaranti.translation_1: Having filled a vessel, I took tuvara and gave it to the Saṅgha.

tuvaraṭṭhinti.meaning_2: a kind of grain (perhaps a measure or preparation of tuvara grain)
tuvaraṭṭhinti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has tuvaraṭṭhinti = tuvaraṭṭhiṃ + iti. The commentary explains tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ. The meaning of aṭṭhi here is uncertain; the PEU entry suggests tuvara + aṭṭhi but gives no distinct sense.
tuvaraṭṭhinti.example_1: Bharitvā tuvaramādāya [bharitvā turavamādāya (ka.), bhajjitaṃ tuvaramādāya (?) ettha tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ tuvaraṭṭhinti tadaṭṭhakathā; tuvaro dhaññabhedeti sakkatābhidhāne], saṅghassa adadiṃ ahaṃ.
tuvaraṭṭhinti.translation_1: Having filled a vessel, I took tuvara and gave it to the Saṅgha.

tuvaro.meaning_2: pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan); a kind of grain; pigeon pea seed
tuvaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (tuvaramādāya). The commentary explains tuvara as a kind of grain like mung or beans; variant reading turava. Spelling here tu- not tu- is the text's own.
tuvaro.example_1: Bharitvā tuvaramādāya [bharitvā turavamādāya (ka.), bhajjitaṃ tuvaramādāya (?) ettha tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ tuvaraṭṭhinti tadaṭṭhakathā; tuvaro dhaññabhedeti sakkatābhidhāne], saṅghassa adadiṃ ahaṃ.
tuvaro.translation_1: Having filled a vessel, I took tuvara and gave it to the Saṅgha.

tuvarassa.meaning_2: pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan); seed of the pigeon pea
tuvarassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text: 'tuvarassa idaṃ phalaṃ' means 'this is the fruit of the pigeon pea (offering)'. Also found as neuter.
tuvarassa.translation_2: I have come to know no bad destination; this is the fruit of the tuvara.

tuvaradāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legends) of the Elder Tuvaradāyaka; Tuvaradāyakathera's Apadāna
tuvaradāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Heading of the first Apadāna; clipped form of tuvaradāyakattherassa apadānaṃ, with the genitive ending in sandhi.

naḷinakesariyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a thera, the speaker of the Apadāna verses; nominative singular in the text.
naḷinakesariyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā naḷinakesariyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

naḷinakesariyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the venerable Naḷinakesariyathera
naḷinakesariyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Continues with the dative/genitive in -ssa and the sandhi -assa + apadānaṃ > -assāpadānaṃ; it is the title line that ends the third story.

viravapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Viravapupphiya Thera; Viravapupphiya Thera's account
viravapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of section 4 of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Viravapupphiya is the monk's name (apparently from virava + pupphiya).

kusaṭṭhakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the elder who gave eight food tickets; story of the senior monastic Kusaṭṭhakadāyaka
kusaṭṭhakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title at the end of a chapter; nominative singular in the text. A compound of kusaṭṭhaka, dāyaka, thera and apadāna (thera + assa as a genitive link).
kusaṭṭhakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.translation_1: The sixth legend of Kusaṭṭhakadāyaka Thera is finished.

sambodhimukhena.meaning_2: leading to full awakening; with full awakening as the means; headed by enlightenment
sambodhimukhena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text: "by that means to awakening". The PEU treats it as a bahubbīhi adjective; the final member is mukha 6/7 in the sense of "headed by; means".
sambodhimukhena.translation_1: because that is the means to awaken, wise, they with sharp knowing, through knowledge and power,

sutikkhapaññā.meaning_2: of very sharp understanding; with thoroughly piercing wisdom; exceedingly wise
sutikkhapaññā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Emphatic prefix su + tikkhapaññā, with the second member in composition (paññā + a). Nominative plural in the first sentence, agreeing with the subject; nom sg (or voc) in the second.
sutikkhapaññā.translation_1: because of their wishes and also great strength, do come to attain that state of omniscience.
sutikkhapaññā.example_2: 85. ‘‘‘ Teneva saṃvegamukhena dhīrā, vināpi buddhehi sutikkhapaññā;
sutikkhapaññā.translation_2: 85. “Because that is the means to awaken, wise, they with sharp knowing, through knowledge and power,

sabbaññubhāvaṃ.meaning_2: state of omniscience; omniscient state; state of the all-knowing one
sabbaññubhāvaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, object of anupāpuṇanti.
sabbaññubhāvaṃ.translation_1: because of their wishes and also great strength, do come to attain that state of omniscience.

buddhattamabhipatthayiṃ.meaning_2: I aspired to Buddhahood; I longed for the state of a Buddha
buddhattamabhipatthayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of buddhattaṃ (accusative) + abhipatthayiṃ (1st person singular aorist). The text reads buddhattam abhipatthayiṃ.
buddhattamabhipatthayiṃ.translation_1: I too among former Buddhas did wish to become a Buddha.

buddhāpadānāni.meaning_2: legends of the Buddhas; life stories of the Buddhas; stories of the Buddha's achievements
buddhāpadānāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural in the text (nominative/accusative plural -āni) with the verb suṇātha. Could also be analysed as buddhānaṃ apadāna, and the PEU records a variant buddhāpadāniya.
buddhāpadānāni.translation_1: Now listen, with purified minds, to the legends of the Buddhas,

suddhamānasā.meaning_2: with a pure mind; of purified heart; possessing a clean mentality
suddhamānasā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative plural in the text, addressing the listeners. bahubbīhi compound describing the audience.
suddhamānasā.translation_1: Now listen, with purified minds, to the legends of the Buddhas,

tiṃsapāramisampuṇṇā.meaning_2: fulfilled with the thirty perfections; complete in the thirty transcendental virtues
tiṃsapāramisampuṇṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of the Buddha; the number is left undeclined in the compound (tiṃsa, not tiṃsāya). Nominative plural in the text, agreeing with dhammarājā. The PeU splits it as tiṃsapāramī + sampuṇṇa.
tiṃsapāramisampuṇṇā.translation_1: innumerable Dhamma-kings who fulfilled thirty perfections.

dasaṅgulī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used of the Buddha's hands. Nominative singular in the text.
dasaṅgulī.translation_1: those World-Chiefs with followers and the Best Buddhas’ Awakening.

vijjantisaṅkhiyā.meaning_2: existing and to be reckoned; that exist and can be counted; as many as exist
vijjantisaṅkhiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vijjanti (present 3rd plural of vijjati 1, 'exist') and saṅkhiyā (nominative plural of the potential participle saṅkhiya, 'to be reckoned'). The phrase ratanā vijjantisaṅkhiyā means 'as many jewels as exist'. Written vijjanti saṅkhiyā in some editions.
vijjantisaṅkhiyā.translation_1: I brought it all forth with my mind: things on the ground and in the sky,

sabbamāhariṃ.meaning_2: I carried off everything; I brought all
sabbamāhariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sabbaṃ (accusative of sabba) and āhariṃ (1st singular aorist of āharati, 'carried here; brought'). The sandhi is -aṃ + ā- > -amā-. In the verse, the speaker gathered all gems, whether in the sky or on the earth, by mind.
sabbamāhariṃ.example_1: Ākāsaṭṭhā ca bhūmaṭṭhā [bhummaṭṭhā (sī. syā.)], manasā sabbamāhariṃ.
sabbamāhariṃ.translation_1: uncountable as are the gems found in the fields of the Buddhas.

rūpiyabhūmiyaṃ.meaning_2: made of silver; with a silver-finished ground; having silver flooring
rūpiyabhūmiyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, describing the palace (pāsādaṃ). The PEU splits it as rūpiyabhūmi + ka, but since the meaning is 'made of silver' the -ya suffix (cf. PEU's kiu) fits better; cf. rūpiya 1 'silver; money'. Could also be read as a tatpuruṣa adjective 'whose ground is silver'.
rūpiyabhūmiyaṃ.translation_1: I created a palace there, with a floor made out of silver.

nekabhummaṃ.meaning_2: having many floors; with many stories
nekabhummaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive adjective modifying a mansion or palace; accusative singular neuter agreeing with the noun in the sentence. Could also be analysed as a bahubbīhi compound ("having many floors").
nekabhummaṃ.translation_1: Various floors made out of gems arose and stretched up toward the sky.

nabhamuggataṃ.meaning_2: risen up into the sky; reaching up to the sky; soaring into the heavens
nabhamuggataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of nabhaṃ (accusative of nabhas, "sky") + uggata (pp of uggacchati, "gone up"). Nominative singular neuter agreeing with vimānaṃ in the second verse; the form in the text could also be read as nominative singular neuter of the compound. The first verse's ubbiddhaṃ agrees similarly.
nabhamuggataṃ.translation_1: Various floors made out of gems arose and stretched up toward the sky.
nabhamuggataṃ.translation_2: and a mansion one hundred and fifty hands wide, raised up into the sky.

vicittathambhaṃ.meaning_2: with diverse pillars; with variegated columns; having multi-coloured posts; lit. variegated pillar
vicittathambhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a building. Nominative singular in the verse, agreeing with the implied structure (sukataṃ, suvibhattaṃ).
vicittathambhaṃ.translation_1: There were varied well-made pillars, well-proportioned, very costly.

kanakamayasaṅghāṭaṃ.meaning_2: golden assemblage; mass made of gold; golden beam
kanakamayasaṅghāṭaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the verse. PEU glosses 'assemblage (such as a beam) made of gold'; the exact architectural referent is uncertain.
kanakamayasaṅghāṭaṃ.translation_1: The central beam was made of gold, the gate was canopy-adorned.

kontacchattehi.meaning_2: parasol topped with a sceptre; sunshade with a lance finial
kontacchattehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text (kontacchattehi). Describes decorated sunshades with lance-like finials; the reading may be connected with kanakacchatta.
kontacchattehi.translation_1: The central beam was made of gold, the gate was canopy-adorned.

vimalabbhasamā.meaning_2: like a stainless cloud; pure as a cloud; lit. stainless cloud like
vimalabbhasamā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Three-part compound; the second member abbha is not given in the related entries. Feminine singular agreeing with bhūmi in the verse.
vimalabbhasamā.translation_1: The first floor, lapis lazuli, was lovely as a stainless cloud.

naḷinakesariyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Naḷinakesariya Thera; Naḷinakesariya Thera's apadāna
naḷinakesariyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Thera is joined by consonant doubling (thera + apadāna > theraapadāna).

kuṭidhūpakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Kuṭidhūpaka; the Apadāna of Elder Kuṭidhūpaka
kuṭidhūpakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fifth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

sattalipupphapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder who offered sattali flowers
sattalipupphapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Sometimes divided sattali-puppha-pūjaka-thera-apadāna.
sattalipupphapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: 8. The legend of the Sattali-flower-offering Thera.

sattalipupphapūjako.meaning_2: one who honoured with sattali flowers; offerer of sattali blossoms
sattalipupphapūjako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name or epithet of a former Buddha's disciple; nominative singular in the text. The PEU glosses sattali as Arabian jasmine.
sattalipupphapūjako.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sattalipupphapūjako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

sattalipupphapūjakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Sattalipupphapūjaka (Offerer of a Sattali Flower); title of the eighth chapter
sattalipupphapūjakattherassāpadānaṃ.construction: sattali + puppha + pūjaka + thera + ssa + apadāna
sattalipupphapūjakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound title at the end of a chapter; nominative singular in -aṃ (nibbacana-style title). Sattali is a flower name; 'pūjaka' means one who honours; 'thera' + genitive 'ssa' = of the Elder. The final -aṃ is the nominative neuter ending.

kiñjakesarā.meaning_2: name of a Universal Monarch; (lit. having a filament-like mane)
kiñjakesarā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name given to a cakkavattī king; nominative plural in the text (caturo kiñjakesarā).
kiñjakesarā.translation_2: “In the sixty-eighth aeon hence, there were four

tuvaranāganaḷinā.meaning_2: Tuvara, Nāga and Nalinā (names of three previous Buddhas)
tuvaranāganaḷinā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] List of Buddha names in the Apadāna verse (with viravī and kuṭidhūpako following); the final element may also be read as nāganaḷinā, a bahubbīhi 'with nāga-lotus'. Treated here as a dvanda of proper names.

dhātusattaliyo.meaning_2: Dhātusattaliya (name of a previous life or rebirth of the Buddha)
dhātusattaliyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of previous existences (Apadāna). Nominative singular in the text; the compound parts are uncertain.
dhātusattaliyo.translation_2: Patta, Dhātu, Sattali, Bimbi, and Uddālaka,

thomakavaggo.meaning_2: chapter on praise; section on laudation
thomakavaggo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the 26th chapter of the Apadāna. Nom. sg. in the text.

thomakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Thomaka Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Thomaka
thomakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the start of the Apadāna; nominative singular in -aṃ. Thomaka is the elder's name.

thomako.meaning_2: name of a monk; the Elder Thomaka; one who praises
thomako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of an Elder (thera) in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.
thomako.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā thomako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

thomakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the elder Thomaka; Thomakatthera's Apadāna
thomakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title: the first Apadāna, of the elder Thomaka. Takes the nominative singular -aṃ as the subject of a heading; the doubling of the s in the text is a sandhi of thera + apadāna.

ticampakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the Elder Ticampakapupphiya; the story of the elder who offered three campaka flowers
ticampakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth apadāna in the Apadāna collection. Nominative singular in the text.

ticampakapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Ticampakapupphiya
ticampakapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title line at the end of the fourth chapter (catutthaṃ). Sandhi of the genitive singular therassa with apadānaṃ; the name means 'the one who offered three campaka flowers'.

yamupāhanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the relative pronoun yaṃ with upāhanaṃ. The text variant yamupāhanaṃ is equivalent to yaṃ upāhanaṃ.
yamupāhanaṃ.example_1: 21. ‘‘ Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ pānadhiṃ [yamupāhanaṃ (sī.), yaṃ pāduṃ (syā.)] dadiṃ tadā;
yamupāhanaṃ.translation_1: 21. In the ninety-one aeons since I donated that shoe back then,

aggapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Aggapupphiya Thera; the story of the elder Aggapupphiya
aggapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. aggappupphiya appears to mean 'having offered the foremost flower'.

thomakekāsanacitakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A string of three names in a list of trees: Thomaka, Ekāsana, Citaka. The -ṃ is the sandhi of the final -ṃ of citakaṃ with the following consonant, or the accusative ending. One could alternatively analyse it as citakaṃ (accusative singular) preceded by the two names in compound.

pādu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Apadāna verse it stands (probably as a gloss variant for pāhano) in a list of names; the spelling pādu is a contracted form of pāda + upadhāna (cf. pādukā).
pādu.example_1: Pānadhi [pāhano (sī.), pādu (syā.)] mañjarī paṇṇaṃ, kuṭido aggapupphiyo;
pādu.translation_1: Pānadhi, Mañjarī, Paṇṇa, Kuṭida, and Aggapupphiya;

kuṭido.meaning_2: name of a Paccekabuddha; giver of a hut; one who offered a hut
kuṭido.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a Paccekabuddha in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Sometimes analysed as kuṭi + dāna, 'offering a hut'.

makkhayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist in the text (yaṃ telaṃ makkhayiṃ = that oil I smeared). PEU splits it as makkha + ṇaya + iṃ, which would make it a causative aorist; the simple causative makkheti fits better. Not a present 3rd singular despite the lemma form.
makkhayiṃ.example_2: 7. ‘‘ Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ telaṃ makkhayiṃ tadā;
makkhayiṃ.translation_2: “In the ninety-four aeons since I smeared that oil then,

aḍḍhacandiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Aḍḍhacandiya Thera; the Apadāna of Elder Aḍḍhacandiya
aḍḍhacandiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Thera's name aḍḍhacandiya is itself a compound (aḍḍha + canda + iya).

mabhiropayiṃ.meaning_2: I offered there; I presented that
mabhiropayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of maṃ (pronoun) + abhiropayiṃ (aorist 1st singular of abhiropeti, 'to cause to ascend; to offer'). The word before is yaṃ canda; some editions read yaṃ pupphaṃ abhiropayiṃ. Used in an Apadāna verse about a flower offering.
mabhiropayiṃ.example_1: 11. ‘‘ Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ canda [yaṃ puppha (ka.)] mabhiropayiṃ;
mabhiropayiṃ.translation_1: In the ninety-two aeons since I offered that [half-moon] flower,

javahaṃsakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Javahaṃsaka Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Javahaṃsaka
javahaṃsakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading, nominative singular in -aṃ. A compound of four members: java (speed), haṃsaka (swan), thera (elder), apadāna (legend). The whole may be analysed as javahaṃsaka + thera + apadāna.

saḷalapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of the elder Saḷalapupphiya
saḷalapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Thera is the Pāḷi form of the Sanskrit sthavira.

heṭhasīlo.meaning_2: of low morals; with a habit of harassing; cruel by nature; of violent conduct
heṭhasīlo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a rakkhasa. Nominative singular in the text.
heṭhasīlo.translation_2: In that place I was a demon, of low morals, terrifying.

biḷālido.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of monks; nominative singular in the text. The second element may be -da (from √dā, 'giver').
biḷālido.example_2: Ukkhipī telacandī ca, dīpado ca biḷālido;
biḷālido.translation_2: Ukkhipī, Tela and Candi, and Dīpado and Biḷālido;

saḷalado.meaning_2: name of a fish; pine tree water monster
saḷalado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Apadāna list of fish names. saḷala = pine tree; da possibly from √dā (give) or √daṃs (bite), or a proper name.
saḷalado.example_2: Maccho javo saḷalado, rakkhaso taraṇo dasa;

taraṇo.meaning_2: name of a mythical being; (lit.) ferryman; one who crosses over
taraṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a list of ten names (dasa) in the Apadāna; the same list calls them rakkhaso, so probably the name of a mythical being. PEU has only taraṇa (nt, boat; crossing) and taraṇi (masc, boat; sun); this form is nominative singular of the masc a-stem taraṇa used as a proper name.

suvaṇṇabibbohaniyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya; the life story of the venerable Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya
suvaṇṇabibbohaniyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. The name Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya means 'one having a golden instruction/pointing-out'. Non-standard sandhi (bibbohaniya + thera > bibbohaniyatthera).

suvaṇṇabibbohaniyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya
suvaṇṇabibbohaniyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular neuter. The thera's name means 'one who has a golden (cover) for the lips' (suvaṇṇa + bibbohaniya).

caṅkoṭakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Caṅkoṭakiya Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Caṅkoṭakiya
caṅkoṭakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a section of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

caṅkoṭakiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the elder Caṅkoṭakiya
caṅkoṭakiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the elder's name in the genitive and āpadānaṃ; title of the third chapter. Appears as a single word in the text.

ambhañjanamadāsahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā. edition) of abbhañjanamadaṃ; sandhi of abbhañjanaṃ (unguent) + adāsaṃ (I gave, aorist of dadāti).
ambhañjanamadāsahaṃ.translation_1: In an immeasurable aeon before this, I gave that unguent then;

cirappo.meaning_2: name of a king; name of an aristocrat (in the time of Buddha Padumuttara)
cirappo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. Nominative singular in the text.
cirappo.example_2: 17. ‘‘ Ito pannarase kappe, cirappo nāma khattiyo;
cirappo.translation_2: In the fifteenth aeon before this, there was an aristocrat named Cirappa,

āluvaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular āluvaṃ in the text. The reading and analysis are uncertain: perhaps āluvā (f.) or āluva (nt); the commentary (Ṇvādi.202) explains it as ala + ṇuva, 'that which clings by creepers'.
āluvaṃ.example_2: Āluvaṃ tassa pādāsiṃ, pasanno sehi pāṇibhi.
āluvaṃ.translation_2: I gave bulbous roots to him, feeling confidence, with my own hands.

caṅkoṭabbhañjanañjalī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] List of three personal names in a Bhikkhāparampara verse; the text may also be read as a dvanda compound (masc, comp). Alternative parsing caṅkoṭa + abbhañjana + añjalī.
caṅkoṭabbhañjanañjalī.translation_2: Suvaṇṇa, Tilamuṭṭhi, and Caṅkoṭa, Abbhañjana, Añjali;

ekajjho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a khattiya in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text as ekajjho. Uncertainty: perhaps from eka + ajjha (one mass), but the name's origin is not certain.
ekajjho.translation_2: In the fifty-seventh aeon, there was an aristocrat called Ekajjha,

massosahaṃ.meaning_2: I heard that; that I heard
massosahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Contracted sandhi of maṃ (or me) + assosahaṃ, 'I heard that'. Alternative resolution me + assosahaṃ.
massosahaṃ.example_1: 18. ‘‘ Ghosa [sadda (sī. syā.)] massosahaṃ tattha, na ca passāmi taṃ jinaṃ;
massosahaṃ.translation_1: 18. I heard the sound there, but I did not see that Victor;

desakittakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Desakittaka
desakittakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -ṃ; the headword is given as it appears in the text.

upasālakanāmohaṃ.meaning_2: named Upasālaka; whose name was Upasālaka
upasālakanāmohaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound used as an adjective describing the brahmin; in the text the form is upasālakanāmohaṃ, adjective + pronoun ahaṃ with sandhi -o + a- > -o-, i.e. upasālakanāmo + ahaṃ. The sandhi has swallowed the final -o of the nominative singular; lemmas of this type are given as upasālakanāma.
upasālakanāmohaṃ.translation_2: 31. “Back then I was a brahmin named Upasālaka.

desamabhikittayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of abhikittayati, here joined in sandhi with desaṃ (desaṃ abhikittayiṃ) but kept as one entry; in the verse it describes praising a region. Could alternatively be analysed as a sandhi form desaṃ + abhikittayiṃ.
desamabhikittayiṃ.translation_2: 34. In the ninety-two aeons before this, when I extolled that region,

desakittakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the elder Desakittaka; Desakittakatthera's Apadāna
desakittakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter/section; nominative singular in the text. Contains thera + assa (genitive of thera) with sandhi.

upāsitvāna.meaning_2: having attended; having honoured; having sat near; having served
upāsitvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of upāsati; used with sambuddhaṃ, 'having attended on the Buddha'. Same meaning as upāsitvā.
upāsitvāna.translation_2: “Attending on the Sambuddha, I performed services;

ambapiṇḍiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Ambapiṇḍiya Thera; the life story of the elder Ambapiṇḍiya
ambapiṇḍiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Ambapiṇḍiya is the name of the elder (ambapiṇḍa + iya, 'mango-lump'). Nominative singular in the text.

saṃsāvakopi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of Pacceka Buddhas (Apadāna verse). In the text -pi is the enclitic 'too' joined to the nominative singular saṃsāvako.
saṃsāvakopi.example_2: Pādo padesaṃ saraṇaṃ, ambo saṃsāvakopi ca;
saṃsāvakopi.translation_2: Pada, Padesa, Saraṇa, Amba and Saṁsāvaka too;
